authoring: Garlic-butter salmon matches the Thu Nov 5, 2026 household card, including 145°F in the thickest part. Nov 8–14 dinners follow the final plan for that week. Sunday has no dinner. Shrimp scampi and Tuscan chicken are not on this week. No nutrition figures are included.

recipes.title: Garlic butter salmon and asparagus
recipes.summary: Sheet-pan salmon for Thursday, Nov 5. Six fillets, asparagus, and a garlic-butter drizzle. Pull it at 145°F.
recipes.authoring: Household seed for Thu Nov 5, 2026. Bake to 145°F in the thickest part.
recipes.safety: Pull the salmon at 145°F in the thickest part.

photo.alt: A side of salmon baked with lemon slices, parsley, and butter on a white platter.
photo.caption: Photograph shows a lemon-baked side of salmon. This recipe uses 6 fillets and roasts asparagus on the same pan.
photo.author: Gatorfan252525
photo.changes: Saved a JPEG whose longest side is 1600 pixels or less.

ingredients.name: salmon fillets
ingredients.note: about 2.5–3 lb total at 6 portions

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: 1 1/2 sticks at 6 portions

ingredients.name: fresh parsley
ingredients.note: or 1 tsp dried parsley at 6 portions

steps.text: Heat the oven to 450°F. Lightly oil a rimmed sheet pan.

timers.label: Oven preheat
timers.note: A reminder while the oven heats. It is not a thermometer.

steps.text: Pat the salmon dry and space the fillets on the pan. Arrange the asparagus around them.
Mix the butter, garlic, parsley, and onion powder.
Spoon that mixture over the salmon and asparagus. Season with the salt and black pepper. Lay lemon slices on top.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, depending on thickness, until the thickest part of the salmon is 145°F. Serve the salmon with the asparagus.

timers.label: Bake
timers.note: Start with 12 minutes. Thick fillets may need the full 15. Pull the salmon at 145°F.

tasks.label: Oil a rimmed sheet pan
Pat the salmon dry
Trim the asparagus
Set out butter, garlic, parsley, and lemon

recipes.title: Crustless pizza bowls
recipes.summary: Monday, Nov 9. Kids have takeout pizza. Grown-ups have crustless bowls with Italian sausage, pepperoni, mushrooms, green pepper, low-sugar marinara, and mozzarella.
recipes.servingsNote: The amounts below are the grown-up batch written in the plan, not a second pizza for the kids. The portion control scales this batch.
recipes.style: Oven, 400°F. The bowls have no crust. Takeout pizza is the kids' dinner.
recipes.authoring: Household plan for Mon Nov 9, 2026. Amounts and the 400°F bake are from that plan.
recipes.safety: Cook the Italian sausage to 160°F before it goes into the bowls. The 15 to 20 minutes in the oven melts the cheese. It is not a substitute for that temperature.
recipes.kidSide: Kids eat takeout pizza. The bowls have no crust.

photo.alt: A sliced supreme pizza with pepperoni, mushrooms, and peppers on a wooden table.
photo.caption: Photograph is a supreme pizza by Scott Bauer, public domain (USDA). It matches the kids' takeout pizza, which has a crust. The grown-up dinner is crustless bowls and is not what this photograph shows.
photo.author: Scott Bauer
photo.changes: Saved a JPEG whose longest side is 1600 pixels or less.

ingredients.name: Italian sausage
ingredients.note: no added sugar

ingredients.name: low-sugar marinara
ingredients.note: half of a 24 oz jar, such as Rao's

ingredients.name: takeout pizza for the kids
ingredients.note: Order it. It is not part of the crustless bowls.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F.

timers.label: Oven preheat
timers.note: A reminder while the oven heats. It is not a thermometer.

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms and the green pepper. Set out oven-safe bowls for the grown-ups.
Brown the Italian sausage in a skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Drain the fat.

timers.label: Check sausage
timers.note: The plan does not set a browning time. Ground sausage is done at 160°F. Keep cooking if it is not there yet.

steps.text: Divide the sausage among the bowls. Add the mushrooms, green pepper, pepperoni, half a jar of low-sugar marinara (12 oz of a 24 oz jar), and the mozzarella.
Bake at 400°F for 15 to 20 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly. The sausage should already be 160°F.

timers.label: Bake bowls
timers.note: Start with 15 minutes. It may need up to 20. The cheese should be bubbly.

steps.text: Serve the kids their takeout pizza. The bowls have no crust.

tasks.label: Set out oven-safe bowls
Slice the mushrooms and green pepper
Order the kids' takeout pizza
Use a low-sugar marinara, and only half the jar

recipes.title: Garlic Parmesan chicken
recipes.summary: Tuesday, Nov 10. Boneless chicken breasts coated with garlic butter, Parmesan, and oregano, with a side salad. The chicken is already on hand.
recipes.servingsNote: About 6 adult portions from about 3 lb of chicken breasts.
recipes.style: Oven, 400°F. Low-carb as written. Side salad for the table.
recipes.authoring: Household plan for Tue Nov 10, 2026. The simple garlic-Parmesan coating is the one written for this week.
recipes.safety: Chicken is done at 165°F in the thickest part.
recipes.kidSide: The side salad is for the table. This dinner has no separate kid starch.

photo.alt: A seasoned chicken breast beside a green salad on a patterned plate.
photo.caption: Photograph by Daderot, CC0. It shows a seasoned chicken breast with a side salad. Tuesday's coating is melted butter, garlic, Parmesan, and oregano, which this photo does not show. The salad in the photo is not dressed with the ranch from this plan.
photo.author: Daderot
photo.changes: Saved a JPEG whose longest side is 1600 pixels.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.note: Already on hand. Check the amount and that it is still safe to cook on Tuesday. Do not buy more for this dinner.

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: melted

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: minced

ingredients.name: grated Parmesan
ingredients.note: check what is already on hand before buying

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: The plan says salt. It does not set a teaspoon amount.

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: A light sprinkle. The plan does not set a teaspoon amount.

ingredients.name: salad greens
ingredients.note: side salad

ingredients.name: ranch dressing
ingredients.note: to serve with the salad

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F.

timers.label: Oven preheat
timers.note: A reminder while the oven heats. It is not a thermometer.

steps.text: Pound the chicken breasts to an even thickness and pat them dry. Season with salt and a light sprinkle of black pepper.
Stir the melted butter, 4 minced garlic cloves, 3/4 cup grated Parmesan, and 1 teaspoon dried oregano. Coat the chicken with that mixture and set it in a baking dish.
Bake at 400°F for 20 to 30 minutes, until the thickest part is 165°F.

timers.label: Bake chicken
timers.note: Start with 20 minutes. It may need up to 30. Chicken is done at 165°F in the thickest part, not when the timer ends.

steps.text: Toss the salad greens with ranch and serve the salad beside the chicken.

tasks.label: Check that the on-hand chicken is still safe to cook
Pound the breasts to an even thickness
Melt the butter and mince 4 garlic cloves
Rinse the salad greens

recipes.title: Garlic butter steak bites
recipes.summary: Wednesday, Nov 11. Sirloin cubes seared with garlic butter and mushrooms, cauliflower mash, and a side salad.
recipes.servingsNote: About 6 adult portions from about 4 lb of sirloin.
recipes.style: Skillet and a pot for the cauliflower. Low-carb as written.
recipes.authoring: Household plan for Wed Nov 11, 2026. Amounts, the sear, and 145°F are from that plan.
recipes.safety: Whole-muscle steak is done at a minimum of 145°F in the center. Rest it at least 3 minutes.
recipes.kidSide: The side salad is for the table. This dinner has no separate kid starch.

photo.alt: Seared steak cubes in a skillet with garlic and herbs.
photo.caption: Artwork made for this app of steak cubes in garlic butter. It is not a photograph from this kitchen. Wednesday's plate also has mushrooms, cauliflower mash, and a side salad, which are not all in this picture.
photo.author: Original artwork for these kitchen apps

ingredients.name: cauliflower
ingredients.note: for mash

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: The plan calls for garlic and does not set a clove count. Use part of the 2 heads on the grocery list.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: The plan does not set a teaspoon amount.

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: The plan does not set a teaspoon amount.

ingredients.name: salad greens
ingredients.note: side salad

ingredients.name: ranch dressing
ingredients.note: to serve with the salad

steps.text: Cut the sirloin into 1-inch cubes and pat them dry. Season with salt and black pepper. Cut the cauliflower into florets and start it steaming. The plan does not set a steam time. Mash it when a fork goes through.
Heat a large skillet until it is very hot. Sear the steak in batches, 2 to 3 minutes a side, so the pan stays hot. The center of a cube should reach at least 145°F.

timers.label: Sear one side
timers.note: One side. Flip and start the timer again. Repeat for the next batch. 145°F in the center is the minimum. The second side may need the full 3 minutes.

steps.text: Move the steak to a plate and rest it at least 3 minutes.

timers.label: Rest steak
timers.note: Rest at least 3 minutes after it reaches 145°F.

steps.text: In the same skillet, melt the 4 tablespoons of butter and cook the garlic and mushrooms until the mushrooms are browned. Spoon that garlic butter over the steak.
Mash the steamed cauliflower. Serve it with the steak, the mushrooms, and a side salad tossed with ranch.

tasks.label: Cut the sirloin into 1-inch cubes and pat it dry
Trim the mushrooms
Cut 2 heads of cauliflower into florets
Rinse the salad greens

recipes.title: Cheesy broccoli ham bake
recipes.summary: Thursday, Nov 12. Diced cooked ham baked with broccoli, cheddar, heavy cream, cream cheese, and garlic.
recipes.servingsNote: About 6 adult portions. The ham is already cooked.
recipes.authoring: Household plan for Thu Nov 12, 2026. Amounts and the 375°F bake are from that plan.
recipes.safety: The ham is already cooked. Bake until the casserole is hot and the cheese is bubbly. This dinner does not start with raw meat.
recipes.kidSide: This dinner has no separate kid starch.

photo.alt: A broccoli and ham casserole with melted cheddar in a baking dish.
photo.caption: Artwork made for this app of a broccoli, ham, and cheese bake. It is not a photograph from this kitchen.
photo.author: Original artwork for these kitchen apps

ingredients.name: diced cooked ham
ingredients.note: already cooked

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: The plan calls for garlic and does not set a clove count. Use part of the 2 heads on the grocery list.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F.

timers.label: Oven preheat
timers.note: A reminder while the oven heats. It is not a thermometer.

steps.text: Cut the broccoli into florets if it is still in crowns. Dice the ham if it is not already diced. The ham is cooked ham.
Stir the cream cheese, heavy cream, and minced garlic together. Fold in the ham, broccoli, and most of the cheddar. Spread it in a baking dish and top with the rest of the cheddar.
Bake at 375°F for 25 to 30 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and the casserole is hot. The ham was already cooked.

timers.label: Bake casserole

recipes.title: Pork carnitas lettuce cups
recipes.summary: Saturday, Nov 14. Slow-cooker pork shoulder shredded and crisped, served in lettuce cups with lime slaw, avocado, and sour cream. Tortillas are for the kids.
recipes.servingsNote: About 6 adult portions from about 5 lb of pork shoulder. The 8 hours on low does not change when you change the portion count.
recipes.style: Slow cooker on low, then a short broil. Low-carb in lettuce cups.
recipes.authoring: Household plan for Sat Nov 14, 2026. Low for 8 hours, then shred and broil.
recipes.safety: Whole cuts of pork are safe at 145°F. This shoulder stays on low for 8 hours so it shreds. It should pull apart easily before you broil it.
recipes.kidSide: Tortillas for the kids. Adults eat lettuce cups.

photo.alt: A white plate piled with shredded cooked pork.
photo.caption: Photograph of shredded pork by Michael J. Bennett, CC BY-SA 3.0. Saturday's dinner is that pork in lettuce cups with lime slaw, avocado, and sour cream. Those sides are not in this photo. Tortillas are only for the kids.
photo.author: Michael J. Bennett

ingredients.note: for cups

steps.text: Put the pork shoulder in the slow cooker with the onion, cumin, chili powder, oregano, and salt. Squeeze in lime. Save some lime for the slaw and the table.
Cook on low for 8 hours, until the pork shreds easily with a fork. Whole cuts of pork are safe at 145°F. This shoulder cooks longer so it pulls apart.

timers.label: Slow cook
timers.note: Low for 8 hours, which is what the plan sets. The end time is saved, so it keeps counting if you leave the page. Check that it shreds. The 8 hours does not change if you change the portion count.

steps.text: Shred the pork.
Spread the shredded pork on a sheet pan and broil until the edges crisp. Stay at the oven. The plan does not set a broil time.

timers.label: Check broiler
timers.note: The plan does not set a broil time. This only tells you to look so it does not burn.

steps.text: Toss the coleslaw mix with lime juice for the slaw.
Serve the pork in lettuce cups with the lime slaw, avocado, sour cream, and cilantro. Warm tortillas only for the kids.

tasks.label: Start the slow cooker in the morning
Slice the onion and set out the spices
Wash the lettuce and save the slaw for serving time
Set tortillas aside only if the kids want them
